title: Query multiplexer + windowed spool cache to smooth dashboard latency spikes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Several customer-facing dashboards show intermittent latency spikes during bursty ingestion and concurrent heavy explorations. Root cause analysis indicates high fanout from identical or highly-overlapping queries issued by the Console UI (filters/time-range/pagination variants) and low reuse of partial results in the current cache layer. Goal: reduce observable latency variance and 95/99th percentiles for dashboard queries without increasing backend cost. Strategy: introduce a lightweight Query Multiplexer service in the dashboard API path that groups similar incoming requests into short-lived micro-batches and routes them to a new Windowed Spool Cache. The spool cache stores semantically hashed partial result sets (by route + filter_signature + time_bucket) and supports multi-request coalescing, soft-cursor merges, and conservative staleness semantics to avoid returning stale telemetry. This ticket covers design, prototype, benchmarking, and a canary rollout for the multiplexer + spool cache integration.
acceptance_criteria: P95 dashboard query latency decreases by >= 25% for monitored routes compared to baseline traffic
P99 latency shows measurable reduction (goal: 15% lower) and fewer >2s spikes across a synthetic burst test
Cache hit-rate for partial results >= 40% on representative workload (first canary)
No data correctness regressions: results must match ground-truth queries within existing tolerance and tests
Rolling canary deployed to 10% of Console traffic with automated rollback on latency or error regressions
technical_decisions: Use a short time-window bucketing approach (spool-window = 120ms) to balance batching latency vs coalescing benefits
Keying scheme: sha256(route + normalized_filter_json + time_bucket) for partial-result entries
Eviction: hybrid LRU + time-based staleness (max TTL 90s) to prevent cache pollution during heavy exploratory queries
Soft-cursors: extend current cursor protocol with a mergeable breadcrumb (cursor_version + digest) so two overlapping paginated requests can be merged without breaking client expectations
No semantic changes to SQL/OLAP engine: multiplexer emits original queries unchanged; spool cache stores serialized partial result fragments at API layer to avoid engine schema coupling
progress_updates: 2025-11-05: Kickoff meeting with ENG, PM, and Observability; initial performance goals agreed
2025-11-08: Prototype multiplexer implemented behind a feature flag; basic spool cache in-memory store with sha256 keys
2025-11-11: Benchmarks vs baseline on local perf harness (2:1 reduction in duplicate queries, P95 improvement ~18% for single-route synthetic burst)
2025-11-13: Design review - noted concerns about memory pressure from spool cache; agreed to implement size-limited shards and admission control
2025-11-15: Implemented shard-level admission control and estimated memory per shard; integrated eviction metrics into staging Grafana
2025-11-18: Canary orchestration plan drafted; PRs opened for multiplexer + instrumentation (see PR links)
Next: Run 10% canary in staging with real traffic replay, collect P50/P95/P99, refine spool-window and TTL
benchmarks: Local perf harness: synthetic workload with 500 concurrent Console sessions replay. Baseline P95=420ms, P99=980ms. Prototype (spool-window=120ms) P95=340ms, P99=840ms. Duplicate query count reduced by 48% in controlled runs. Memory: spool cache steady-state ~120MB per shard under replay workload (configurable).
metrics_baseline: Dashboard-api routes monitored: p50=85ms, p95=420ms, p99=980ms, avg duplicate-query-rate=22% (same route/signature within 500ms window)
risks: Spool cache memory growth under pathological exploratory queries - mitigated by shard admission control and TTL
Potential increased tail latency if spool-window is tuned too large - controlled via canary and dynamic adjustment
Correctness concerns for pagination when results shift between spool windows - mitigated by conservative soft-cursor merging and integration tests
notes_for_rollout: 1) Feature flag gated with config knob for spool-window and TTL. 2) Start 1% traffic canary -> 10% if no regressions after 30m -> 50% -> 100%. 3) Automated rollback triggers: error-rate + latency SLO breaches or cache memory above shard threshold. 4) Expose runtime metrics: spool_window_latency, spool_cache_hit_rate, admission_drop_rate, merged_query_count
next_steps: Run staging 10% replay and collect extended metrics (24h)
Tune spool-window and TTL from staging results
Add integration tests that validate soft-cursor merges across paginated requests
Prepare runbook for on-call teams and update Console troubleshooting doc
